Thought: I need to determine the correct ordering of compounds in terms of increasing wavenumber of the carbonyl stretching mode. The wavenumber of the carbonyl stretching mode is affected by the electron-withdrawing or electron-donating properties of the substituents attached to the carbonyl group.

In this case, we're looking at compounds with the structure O=C(CX₃)C₆H₅, where X is a halogen (F, Cl, Br, or I). The more electron-withdrawing the CX₃ group is, the higher the wavenumber of the carbonyl stretching mode will be.

The electronegativity of halogens decreases down the group: F > Cl > Br > I. Therefore, CF₃ is the most electron-withdrawing group, followed by CCl₃, CBr₃, and CI₃.

The more electron-withdrawing the group, the higher the wavenumber of the carbonyl stretching mode. So the order of increasing wavenumber should be:

O=C(C(I)(I)I)C₆H₅ < O=C(C(Br)(Br)Br)C₆H₅ < O=C(C(Cl)(Cl)Cl)C₆H₅ < O=C(C(F)(F)F)C₆H₅

Looking at the options, I need to find the one that matches this order or a portion of it.

Option A: O=C(C(Br)(Br)Br)C₆H₅ < O=C(C(I)(I)I)C₆H₅ < O=C(C(F)(F)F)C₆H₅
This is incorrect because it places CBr₃ before CI₃, but I is less electronegative than Br.

Option B: O=C(C(Cl)(Cl)Cl)C₆H₅ < O=C(C(F)(F)F)C₆H₅ < O=C(C(I)(I)I)C₆H₅
This is incorrect because it places CI₃ after CF₃, but I is less electronegative than F.

Option C: O=C(C(F)(F)F)C₆H₅ < O=C(C(I)(I)I)C₆H₅ < O=C(C(Cl)(Cl)Cl)C₆H₅
This is incorrect because it places CF₃ before CI₃, but F is more electronegative than I, so CF₃ should have a higher wavenumber.

Option D: O=C(C(I)(I)I)C₆H₅ < O=C(C(Cl)(Cl)Cl)C₆H₅ < O=C(C(F)(F)F)C₆H₅
This matches our expected order (at least for the compounds listed). I is less electronegative than Cl, which is less electronegative than F, so the wavenumber increases in this order.
Final Answer: [ANSWER]D[/ANSWER]
